subject.title: fix: inject only shared auth into macos dashboard

question: Should macOS Dashboard browser auth injection be restricted to configured shared token/password auth, including endpoint-change reloads, or may it inject native device tokens for Dashboard parity?
rationale: This PR and the sibling native-token parity PR implement conflicting credential boundaries, and the choice affects upgrade behavior plus whether native device tokens can cross into the embedded browser Control UI.

options.title: Use shared-token-only browser injection
options.body: Confirm the security boundary, update all Dashboard open/reload paths to shared-token-only auth, and close or redirect the sibling parity direction.

options.title: Allow native-token Dashboard parity
options.body: Accept native device tokens in the embedded browser path and pause or close this PR in favor of the parity branch.

options.title: Pause both branches for a documented policy
options.body: Keep both draft PRs blocked until the macOS Dashboard auth policy is documented and tested against fresh-install and upgrade behavior.

recommendation.title: Use shared-token-only browser injection
recommendation.body: Confirm the security boundary, update all Dashboard open/reload paths to shared-token-only auth, and close or redirect the sibling parity direction.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete owns the recent Dashboard endpoint reload behavior and much of the native Dashboard history touched by this auth-boundary choice.
